materiality_analysis.reason: The 2025 disclosure introduces a significant new risk factor not present in 2024: 'server revenue was limited in Q4 2025 by our available supply of products due to Intel Foundry wafer fabrication supply constraints... expected to persist into 2026.' This moves from a discussion of demand/pricing drivers to a specific supply-side constraint limiting revenue, which is a material change in the company's operational and financial exposure.

comparisons.peer_summary: Data Center net revenue increased 94% to $12.6 billion in 2024 from $6.5 billion in 2023, primarily driven by higher sales of AMD Instinct GPUs and AMD EPYC CPUs. Operating income rose to $3.5 billion in 2024 from $1.3 billion in 2023, mainly due to higher revenue partially offset by increased R&D investment.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies report on the financial drivers for their data center/server businesses, but they present opposing performance trajectories regarding ASPs and volume. Intel's DCAI revenue was stagnant (+1%) because higher ASPs from high-core-count products were offset by lower volume. In contrast, AMD's Data Center segment saw massive growth (+94%) driven by higher sales volume and ASPs of Instinct GPUs and EPYC CPUs, indicating strong demand outpacing any price pressure or volume decline seen at Intel.

sentences.text: DCAI revenue increased 1% from 2023 driven by higher server revenue primarily from high core count products, which increased ASPs and lowered volume compared to 2023.
Data Center net revenue of $12.6 billion in 2024 increased by 94%, compared to net revenue of $6.5 billion in 2023.
The increase was primarily driven by higher sales of AMD Instinct GPUs and AMD EPYC CPUs.

comparisons.peer_summary: CNBU operating income improved in 2024 compared to 2023, driven by higher bit shipments, increased average selling prices, and cost reductions, partially offset by higher R&D expenses.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Micron (CNBU) disclose that average selling prices (ASPs) increased in 2024 compared to 2023. However, the drivers and outcomes differed: Intel's ASP increase was associated with lower volume and resulted in only flat total revenue, whereas Micron's CNBU ASP increases, combined with higher bit shipments, contributed to improved operating income.
